name: Belgian French
notes: Belgian French as a thin variant of Metropolitan French (fr-FR). One feature is stated, from the PFC survey of Tournai: patte ≠ pâte is kept as a difference of LENGTH, so ⟨â⟩ is [ɑː] here and [ɑ] in fr-FR (PFC page, d) 1) La distinction /a/-/ɑ/: 'patte ≠ pâte (opposition de longueur): Suisse : Neuchâtel - Belgique : Tournai'). The /ɛ̃/ ~ /œ̃/ contrast (brin ≠ brun, a very slight timbre difference at Tournai, PFC page d) 2)) is kept as in fr-FR, which writes ⟨un⟩ [œ̃] and ⟨in⟩ [ɛ̃] apart and keeps [ɛ̃] as an allophone of /œ̃/. NOT MODELLED: the vowel length opposition for other vowels, the PFC remark that the ⟨ê⟩ ~ ⟨e⟩ length contrast is documented for Neuchâtel and not stated for Belgium, regional vowel quality, the weakening of /e/ ~ /ɛ/ and /o/ ~ /ɔ/ among young speakers, and the numerals septante and nonante (numbers are out of scope). The page is a survey summary at one point (Tournai) and not a description of every Belgian variety.

sources.author: Projet PFC (Phonologie du français contemporain), FLORAL-PFC
sources.title: Le français expliqué: Prononciation, I. Le système vocalique, d) Variation
sources.notes: READ (open web page; the page metadata gives 2010 as its publication year and 2017 as its last change). The page reports, from PFC survey points: patte ≠ pâte by LENGTH at Neuchâtel (Switzerland) and Tournai (Belgium) and by timbre at Nyon; patte = pâte at Brunoy and Abidjan; brin ≠ brun kept at Tournai and Nyon (very slight timbre difference), at Toulouse and Abidjan (marked), and fading among young speakers at Neuchâtel; the length opposition faites [fɛt] ~ fête [fɛːt], belle ~ bêle, nu ~ nue, vit ~ vie at Neuchâtel. The page cites Gadet (1996) and Léon (2007).

ancestors.notes: Standard Metropolitan French, the base of every other variety here.
